As the UAE authorities continue their investigation into the circumstances surrounding the flydubai flight incident, they have cautioned against oversimplifying the incident, speculation or premature conclusions before the investigation is completed. At the same time, Captain Smit’s courage and swift response during the incident continues to draw praise from across the UAE.The UAE’s civil aviation regulator, the General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA) said that investigation into the incident is continuing under approved procedures, with confidentiality and integrity; and in coordination with relevant regional and international authorities. The GCAA said it would not comment on details or claims in circulation that could pre-empt the findings or affect the course of the investigation at this stage. It urged the public to refrain from circulating speculation or unverified information. GCAA commended the courage and swift response of Captain Smit, the crew and passengers.Flydubai Chief Executive Officer Ghaith Al Ghaith said all passengers and crew on board are safe and being cared for. He thanked the captain, the pilots who secured and landed the aircraft, the cabin crew and passengers who assisted during the challenging situation. Flydubai has temporarily suspended its operations to Tel Aviv at the request of the authorities while the investigation continues. He acknowledged that there are many questions about what happened on board FZ1073, saying a full official investigation is underway to establish the facts. He said flydubai is fully supporting the investigation and stressed the importance of allowing the process to take its course.Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the President of UAE, also praised Captain Smit’s bravery. In a social media post, he said the Indian pilot demonstrated courage and responsibility in confronting what he described as a dangerous terrorist act and a potential disaster. He also cautioned against oversimplifying the incident or promoting conspiracy theories, stressing the need for vigilance and caution in addressing the risks of extremism and terrorism.

. The UAE Attorney-General, Counsellor Dr Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, has said investigations into the flydubai flight FZ1073 incident found that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a terrorist act.Emirates News Agency (WAM) quoted Al Shamsi saying the co-pilot began executing his plan during the flight by attacking the captain inside the flight deck with a crash axe and attempting to take control of the aircraft.Investigations are continuing to establish the full circumstances and motives behind the incident, as well as any links, while technical examinations and analysis of physical and digital evidence are also underway. The Attorney-General said the final findings will be announced upon conclusion of all necessary procedures.

. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to light the ceremonial flame at Israel’s upcoming Independence Day celebrations.During a telephone conversation with Captain Machchhar, Mr Netanyahu praised the Indian pilot as a hero of India, Israel and the world for his bravery in foiling a mid-air attack. He also wished Captain Machchhar a speedy and complete recovery and conveyed his best wishes to the pilot’s family. Mr Netanyahu noted that the honour of lighting the ceremonial flame is traditionally reserved for Israeli citizens, making the invitation a rare and significant recognition of Captain Machchhar’s courage and service.Captain Machchhar, who is currently in Abu Dhabi receiving medical care and undergoing recovery, displayed extraordinary courage and presence of mind in saving the lives of 174 passengers during an attack in the cockpit.

. The Ministry of Education has approved five Centres of Excellence for studies in classical languages. Department of Higher Education has approved the establishment of the five Centres of Excellence for studies in Classical Assamese, Classical Bengali, Classical Marathi, Classical Pali and Classical Prakrit.The Centres of Excellence will be established at Tezpur University in Assam, Visva-Bharati University in West Bengal, Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in Pune, Central University of Odisha, and Central University of Gujarat. The initiative will provide dedicated institutional support for advanced academic research, preservation and digitisation of linguistic and literary heritage, and wider dissemination of knowledge relating to these Classical Languages. The establishment of these five Centres marks a significant step towards strengthening the institutional ecosystem for the study, research and preservation of India’s Classical Languages.

. The National Statistics Office (NSO), is conducting the Forward-Looking Survey on Private Corporate Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions (CAPEX 2026) during the period of October to December 2026.The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said that the survey is aimed at generating comprehensive and timely information on capital expenditure undertaken and planned by large private corporate sector enterprises. The Ministry added that the survey will provide important inputs for understanding emerging investment trends in the Indian economy.The primary objective of the CAPEX Survey is to collect information on capital expenditure undertaken in the recent financial years , provisional capital expenditure in the current financial year and investment intentions for the forthcoming financial year.The Ministry has appealed all the selected private corporate sector enterprises to extend their full cooperation and participate actively in the CAPEX 2026 Survey.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the Men’s Cricket Team on retaining their title at the Asian Games 2026. In a series of social media post, Mr Modi said that this is indeed a joyous occasion for the nation. He also wished the team members for their future endeavours.Mr Modi said the 2026 Asian Games have been truly special for Indian Hockey. He congratulated the Men’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asian Games Gold with a commanding victory in the final. He said it has been an exceptional campaign by the players, with back-to-back Asian Games Golds for the first time and a fifth Gold overall. He said the triumph becomes even more special as, for the first time, both Indian Men’s and Women’s Hockey Teams have won Gold at the same Asian Games. He stated that it is clear that Indian Hockey stands tall on the Asian stage.The Prime Minister also congratulated Pranavi Sharath Urs on winning India’s first-ever Gold in Women’s Individual Golf at the Asian Games. Mr Modi said that her superb finish has given the nation a sporting moment to remember. He wished that the victory would draw more young Indians to the game and inspire them to aim for the very top.Mr Modi also congratulated Kumkum Anil Mohod on becoming the first Indian woman to win Recurve Individual Gold at the 2026 Asian Games. He said that her composure in the decisive shoot-off was particularly outstanding. The Prime Minister wished her for future endeavours, and called her to keep aiming higher.Prime Minister also congratulated Aman Sehrawat for scripting history by winning India’s first-ever Asian Games Gold in the Men’s 57kg Freestyle Wrestling event. He added that from Bronze at the last Asian Games to standing atop the podium this time, Aman has displayed great tenacity.Mr Modi expressed happiness that six decades later, India is back on the podium in the Men’s 97kg Freestyle Wrestling event at the Asian Games. He said, Deepak Punia brought home the Bronze after a fiercely contested bout, adding a new chapter to India’s wrestling journey.

. A crash involving multiple vehicles on the highway to the Kenyan coastal city of Mombasa today killed 17 people, most of them pilgrims on the way to a prayer site. Police said, the crash in the Salama area happened when a truck driver tried and failed to overtake another truck.The van’s driver and 16 passengers, most of them women, died at the scene. The pilgrims were going to a prayer site in Nakuru County, west of the Kenyan capital of Nairobi. President William Ruto offered condolences to the families.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by 18.3 billion US dollars (USD) to 747.5 billion US dollars during the week ended the 25th of September. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 15.5 billion USD to 615.4 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 2.5 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 97 million USD to 18.64 billion USD. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped by 86 million to 4.8 billion USD.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey asserted that India needs capital markets that can mobilise capital, manage risk and build investor confidence.While addressing the 12th International Convention of the Commodity and Capital Market Participants Association of India in New Delhi today, he said, the regulator is working to strengthen the market structure so that households can invest with confidence, businesses can raise funds for growth, and market intermediaries maintain high standards of conduct. SEBI Chairman said, the regulator is examining concerns related to the settlement price framework for derivatives on expiry days following the introduction of the Closing Auction Session – CAS. The mechanism was introduced to improve price discovery for eligible stocks at market close by using a call-auction process to determine a single equilibrium price instead of relying solely on volume-weighted average prices.He also said, SEBI is working to deepen and improve liquidity in cash markets, expand participation and strengthen securities borrowing and lending. He added that efficient hedging and arbitrage can improve price discovery and strengthen the interaction between cash and derivatives markets. The regulator is also examining position limits for non-agricultural contracts with the aim of improving market liquidity and depth while maintaining risk controls.

. Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah has said that the Narendra Modi government is developing a complete ecosystem around cattle rearing, from converting cow dung into biogas and organic fertiliser to processing dairy products and providing market access, to give a new boost to the rural economy. Addressing the state-level Gau Palak Sammelan in Bhopal today, Mr Shah said cattle rearers would be among those benefiting the most from the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation.On criminal justice reforms, Mr Shah said that once the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita is fully implemented, India’s criminal justice system will become the most modern in the world. He said that after full implementation of the BNS, cases could be disposed of within three years, from the registration of an FIR to the Supreme Court.

. India won five gold, two silver and two bronze medals at the Asian Games in Japan today.In Hockey, India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 to defend their men’s gold and the triumph also secured them a direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. For India, captain Harmanpreet Singh netted two goals while Jugraj, Hardik and Shilanand scored one goal each.In Men’s Cricket, India won the gold defeating arch-rivals Pakistan by 19 runs in the T20 final at Nisshin.Wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final. Kumkum Mohod won the individual gold medal in the women’s recurve archery event.In Golf, Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s individual title. India also bagged silver in the team event.Wrestler Antim Panghal sealed a silver medal in the women’s 53 kg category.Deepak Punia won bronze in the men’s 97kg freestyle wrestling event after defeating Mongolia’s Gankhuyag Ganbaatar.  Archer Neeraj Chauhan got bronze in the men’s individual recurve event.With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fourth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 85, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals.

. Five Indian nationals were rescued after a Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. The Indian Embassy in Oman said in a post on X today that it coordinated the rescue of the five Indians on board the MT Kazimah III, who were safely brought ashore. The mission thanked Omani authorities for their continued support and assistance during the rescue operation.Several commercial vessels carrying Indian seafarers have come under attack amid escalating tensions in West Asia. The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. The United States has designated 50 countries whose citizens face visa bonds reaching up to 20,000 US Dollars for tourist and business visas, leaving India exempt from the mandate while encompassing South Asian nations such as Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal.The State Department released a revised list of nations yesterday whose nationals must post financial bonds upon qualifying for B1/B2 visas. Under this programme, individuals travelling on passports from the specified countries are required to deposit bonds valued at 10,000, 15,000 or 20,000 US Dollars with the exact figure fixed by a consular official during the visa interview.Holders of Indian passports remain exempt from this obligation. As detailed by the State Department index, Nepal and Bangladesh have faced the mandate since January 21, whereas Bhutan was incorporated beginning January 1. Additional nations spanning Africa, the Caribbean, Central Asia and the Pacific are similarly featured.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has reconstituted several Parliamentary Committees related to different Ministries. BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab has been appointed as a chairperson of the Committee on Finance, comprising 21 members from Lok Sabha and 10 members of Rajya Sabha.Mr Birla has appointed Congress MP Shashi Tharoor as chairperson of the Committee on External Affairs. It includes 21 members from lower house and 10 from upper house. While the committee on Railways will be headed by BJP MP Sudhir Gupta. Mr Birla has appointed Lok Sabha MP Dr. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as chairperson of Committee on Chemicals and Fertilizers.Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi will be the chairperson of Committee on Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Food Processing, BJP MP Radha Mohan Singh will be the chairperson of the Committee on Defence; BJP MP Rajiv Pratap Rudy has been appointed as a chairperson of the Committee on Water Resources, while the Committee on Rural Development and Panchayati Raj will be headed by the Congress MP Saptagiri Ulaka. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey has been appointed as the chairperson of the Committee on Communications and Information Technology.The term of these Committees will be effective from 26th of last month.

. Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) has completed one year today. The PM-SETU scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was launched on 4th of October last year. The initiative seeks to strengthen industry-led governance, upgrade training infrastructure and promote demand-driven courses in line with evolving workforce requirements.It aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training by transforming Government India’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into modern, industry-aligned training institutions. The scheme has a total outlay of over 60 thousand crore rupees, comprising 30 thousand crore rupees from the Centre, 20 thousand crore rupees from States and 10 thousand crore rupees from industry.ITIs provide vocational training to equip youth with practical skills for employment and industry. Under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), training is offered through Government and Private Industrial Training Institutes in engineering and non-engineering trades. Its course duration varies from six months to two years, depending on the trade. The Directorate General of Training is the apex organisation responsible for the development and coordination of vocational training at the national level.The total number of ITIs, including Government and Private, in the country has increased to over 13 thousand in 2026 from over nine thousand in 2014, indicating an increase of 42 percent. Further, enrolment in ITIs across the country has also increased to 14.70 lakh in the academic session 2025-26 from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014-15, indicating an increase of 54 percent.At the national level, the Ministry has constituted a National Steering Committee (NSC) to provide overall direction for the scheme. Since its implementation, 850 ITIs have been identified, comprising 172 Hub ITIs and 678 Spoke ITIs. The NSC has also approved the transition of PM-SETU from its pilot phase to a nationwide rollout across all 200 identified ITI clusters. The rollout enables States and Union Territories to take up implementation based on industry readiness and implementation capacity. Approval has been given to Strategic Investment Plans for 14 ITI clusters under PM-SETU with an investment of over 3 thousand 446 crore rupees.

. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman golfer to win a gold medal in the Asian Games, holding on to a slender one-stroke lead in the final round to achieve the historic feat. She also helped the country claim the team silver.The 23-year-old from Mysore sent in three birdies to recover from a horrendous triple bogey on the third hole, which had wiped away her three-stroke overnight lead. With a final round score of even-par 70, she ended with a total of 15-under 265 for four days, a stroke ahead of the pack.Her performance also became a crucial factor in giving India the team silver alongside Aditi Ashok (67 in final round) and Diksha Dagar (77 in final round). Pranavi’s medal was India’s first gold since the 2002 men’s individual top honours bagged by Shiv Kapur.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have paid tribute to freedom fighter Shyamji Krishna Varma on his birth anniversary today.In a social media post, the Vice President said that his unwavering commitment to India’s freedom, fearless spirit and pioneering efforts to inspire and nurture revolutionary nationalism among Indians abroad remain an enduring part of India’s freedom struggle. Mr Radhakrishnan added that his life and sacrifice continue to inspire generations to serve the nation with courage, conviction and dedication.Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, Shyamji Krishna Varma dedicated his entire life for the freedom of India. The Prime Minister added that the nation will forever remember his courage and devotion in safeguarding the honor of the motherland.

. US President Donald Trump dismissed the prospect of implementing a restriction on US diesel shipments following commitments from European nations to expand fuel availability within the market, asserting that the supplementary volume would assist in lowering energy costs.Speaking to reporters at the White House, Mr. Trump noted that he had personally appealed to Europe to increase diesel provisions. Connecting the anticipated rise in supply to the ongoing situation involving Iran, the President expressed confidence that petroleum costs would decline once the conflict concluded.When questioned subsequently regarding whether a ban on diesel outbound shipments was permanently averted as a result of the European action, Mr. Trump clarified that his administration had never planned such a measure.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices declined sharply by over 1.5% today. The Sensex plunged 1,240 points to close at 72,772. The Nifty shed 360 points to settle at 22 thousand 780. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tumbled 1.6%, while the Smallcap 100 index tanked 1.8%.In the Sensex pack, 29 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses, with Infosys emerging as the lone gainer, rising 0.2%. Among the top underperformers, Larsen and Toubro slumped 2.8%, PowerGrid declined 2.6%, and Adani Ports fell 2.4%.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged lower. Among the top laggards,PSU Banks skidded 3.2%, Power, Telecommunication, and Utilities lost 2.3% each and Mid-Small Private Banks dropped 2.2%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 3218 companies declined, 1271 advanced and 228 remained unchanged.

. The All India Consumer Products Federation and the All India Mobile Retailers Association have decided to withdraw their proposed call for a ‘No UPI Day’ on Friday.The decision was taken following a meeting between a delegation of around 20 senior trade leaders, led by BJP MP and Secretary General of the Confederation of All India Traders, Praveen Khandelwal, and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi. During the meeting, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman assured the delegation that the government remains committed to promoting digital transactions while safeguarding the interests of all stakeholders.The trade leaders reiterated their full support for the Digital India mission and the success of UPI, which has emerged as a global model for digital payments. The delegation expressed confidence that continued dialogue between the government and trade bodies would help evolve a practical and sustainable framework to further strengthen India’s digital economy.

. British-Indian chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has been recognised by Guinness World Records as the youngest chess player to achieve the Woman Grandmaster (WGM) title. The 11-year-old London schoolgirl made history at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, becoming the youngest player ever to earn the coveted WGM title.The achievement gives Bodhana three Guinness World Records titles. Her earlier records include being the youngest chess Woman International Master and the youngest female player to defeat a grandmaster in a chess tournament.Bodhana said the recognition is a huge honour and a morale boost, motivating her to continue improving and achieve more. Her journey into chess began at the age of five years and eight months, after she developed a fascination with the knight chess piece. She went on to win competitions by the age of six.Guinness World Records Editor-in-Chief Craig Glenday described Bodhana’s story as an inspiring example of how childhood curiosity and passion can lead to extraordinary achievements.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan today paid tributes to martyr Subramania Siva on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, the Vice President said that Subramania Siva made the call for freedom, Vande Mataram, echo across every nook and corner of Tamil Nadu and awaken the yearning for freedom in the hearts of the people.Mr. Radhakrishnan noted that through his fiery speeches and heroic writings, Subramania Siva rallied the people against foreign rule. He said that without regard for the torments of imprisonment or the afflictions of ill health, Subramania Siva dedicated his entire life to the cause of national liberation.The Vice President added that the unyielding patriotism, spirit of sacrifice, and spirit of liberation that Subramania Siva instilled among the people should endure forever, continuing to inspire every generation to work with dedication for the welfare of the nation.

. In the Asian Games, India won the gold in Men’s cricket, defeating arch-rivals Pakistan in the T20 cricket final at Nisshin, Japan, today. India won the final by 19 runs. Chasing India’s target of 212 runs, Pakistan managed to score only 196 for six in their stipulated 20 overs.Earlier, India posted 211 for six after opting to bat first. Opener Abhishek Sharma scored 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls. Shivam Dube added 27 off 14 balls to take India past the 200-run mark. For Pakistan, Hasan Nawaz scored 96 runs while left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas and pacer Ahmed Daniyal took two wickets each.

. India’s registered manufacturing sector recorded strong growth in financial year 2025 (FY25), with industrial output rising 7.81 per cent and total employment increasing almost 7.2 per cent over the previous year.According to the Annual Survey of Industries data released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation today, the total number of establishments in this sector increased from 2.60 lakh in FY24 to 2.67 lakh in FY25, representing a growth of 2.64 per cent. The highest number of establishments was reported in Tamil Nadu, followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra.Meanwhile, total emoluments paid to the workforce also increased by over 12 per cent in 2024-25 on an annual basis. Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana have emerged as the top 5 states in employment, having a share of more than 56 per cent of the total manufacturing employment of the country in FY25.

. NITI Aayog Member Rajiv Gauba has emphasised the need for regulatory frameworks to evolve alongside a rapidly changing geopolitical, technological and economic environment. He emphasised that the challenge before policymakers is not to choose between regulation and growth, but to develop regulations that manage risks while supporting innovation, competition and investment. Mr Gauba stated this while addressing the plenary session on “Regulatory Oversight in an Age of Disruption” at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi yesterday.Emphasising the need for a proportionate approach, Mr Gauba said regulatory requirements should be calibrated to the nature and consequences of the risks involved. He noted that regulators must carefully assess whether new rules are warranted before intervening in new and rapidly evolving sectors and avoid attempting to prescribe solutions for every possible failure. He also called for greater coordination among regulators to address overlapping mandates, avoid duplication and close regulatory gaps as businesses increasingly operate across traditional regulatory domains.

. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 are set to conclude today, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end. The closing ceremony will be held at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan, the same venue that hosted the opening ceremony, and is scheduled to begin at 6 PM IST.India has put up an impressive performance at this year’s Games, securing fourth place in the overall medal standings with a tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.India’s women’s flag-bearer for the closing ceremony has been confirmed as shooting star Neeru Dhanda, who will proudly carry the Tricolour in Nagoya. The ceremony will feature traditional closing proceedings, including the parade of athletes and the formal conclusion of the Games.

. The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave will be held from this Saturday in New Delhi, under the theme of ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’. The Ministry of Finance said that the three-day gathering will bring together more than 180 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries.The Ministry added that the Conclave will feature plenary sessions, interactive parallel sessions and roundtables. The roundtables will focus on issues including attracting foreign direct investment and mobilising domestic capital for long-term investment. The Ministry said that these roundtables will provide opportunities for more focused exchanges among policymakers, economists, investors and practitioners.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will deliver the inaugural address on the first day of the conclave. The conclave will also witness addresses from Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other Union Ministers. The Ministry informed that the conclave will also feature a special address by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Sanjay Malhotra.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today chaired a consultative committee meeting on India – Russia relations in New Delhi. During the meeting, Dr Jaishankar highlighted various aspects of India’s multifaceted engagement, including in trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and P2P domains.In a social media post, the External Affairs Minister said, he also highlighted India’s active support for dialogue and diplomacy to end the Ukraine conflict.

. Ukraine has described India’s proposal for a possible ceasefire with Russia as the broadest among four offers received by Kyiv, with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha saying it is ready to consider a truce covering energy infrastructure and the Black Sea.  The Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year, has killed thousands of civilians, displaced millions and caused widespread destruction of homes and critical infrastructure.The comments came a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has very good ideas for finding a mutually acceptable settlement to the Ukraine conflict. Sybiha said the proposals for a possible ceasefire had come from India, Turkiye, Egypt and the United States. He said, Kyiv is ready to consider different formats for a truce, but any agreement should cover not only combat operations but also attacks on energy and port infrastructure and the situation in the Black Sea.

. Indian wrestler Aman Sehrawat clinched the men’s 57kg gold after edging out North Korea’s world champion Chong Song Han 11-7 in a fierce final in Asian Games at Nagoya in Japan today. The 23-year-old Indian, who had won a bronze at the Hangzhou Asian Games, showed immense tactical acumen to thwart a tricky Han and complete his climb to the top of the podium. Aman’s gold also adds to India’s strong showing in wrestling after Sujeet Kalkal won men’s 65kg gold yesterday.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 13, clinching SIX gold medals – in Hockey, Boxing, Wrestling and Archery – in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence.The Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title.Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event.In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final.India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final.In Archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final.India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final.In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event.In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event.With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 76, including 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.President Dropadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have congratulated medal winners.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today said that India’s economic strength and resilience have been built over the past decade through a combination of fiscal prudence, infrastructure investment, banking reforms, improved delivery mechanisms and consistent reforms.Addressing the 5th Kautilya economic conclave in New Delhi, the Finance Minister said that the government has advanced the national frameworks through GST, insolvency and bankruptcy code and the four labour codes. She said that India had navigated the shocks of the past four years with its fundamentals intact, citing 7.8 percent real GDP growth in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27.The Finance Minister said that the IMF projects India’s general government debt to decline from 83.4 percent of GDP in 2026 to 77.7 percent in 2031 against a rising global trend.On infrastructure development, Ms Sitharaman said, capital expenditure for this fiscal had been budgeted at 12.22 lakh crore rupees. She added that the national highway network had expanded by about 61 per cent and the number of operational airports had more than doubled since 2014.She also highlighted that more than 52 crore collateral-free loans have been sanctioned under PM MUDRA Yojana. Highlighting the PM Awas Yojana, PM Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, Ms Sitaharaman said that these initiatives have strengthened citizens’ capacity to participate in growth and build capacities to fight the challenges.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. In the Asian Games, Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan upset compatriot Dhiraj Bommadevara 6-4 to bag the bronze medal in the men’s individual recurve event in Nagoya, Japan, today. Neeraj became only the second Indian male after Tarundeep Rai to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Earlier, top seed Dhiraj went down 3-7 to Paris Olympics bronze medallist Lee Woo Seok in the first semifinal, while Neeraj was outplayed 1-7 by Japanese archer Junya Nakanishi in his last-four stage match. Dhiraj had defeated Uzbekistan’s Amirkhon Sadikov in the quarterfinals, while Neeraj advanced to the semifinals defeating Bhutan’s Lam Dorji.

Dubai Crown Prince, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence for the UAE, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, visited Captain Smit Machchhar, the flydubai pilot involved in the FZ1073 incident.In a post following the visit, Sheikh Hamdan praised Captain Smit for demonstrating “the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life.” He added that the UAE was proud to have Captain Smit as part of its team and its story.Sheikh Hamdan also described the pilot as representing what the UAE stands for — “a nation of compassion, a nation of peace, and a nation of life.”

Ministry of External Affairs has summoned the Chargé d’Affaires of Pakistan High Commission to lodge India’s strong protest over the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan. India also categorically rejected the baseless and motivated allegations regarding an incident in the Ferozepur sector, Punjab, along the International Border on Friday.External Affairs Ministry said that the Pakistani side was informed that three individuals infiltrated into Indian territory and despite multiple warnings by BSF to return to Pakistan, continued to move towards the border fence. The BSF was compelled to engage them for posing an imminent security threat. India said this incident highlights a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan. Pakistan was urged to investigate these cross-border infiltration and drug smuggling activities and the complicity of Pakistan Border Guarding forces and to take appropriate remedial measures.Islamabad was further urged to ensure respect for the sanctity of the International Border, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements, mandate its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorised movement from its side, and take definitive measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

The gold rush continued for India at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance on Day 14, clinching 17 gold medals in Boxing, Wrestling and Archery in a spectacular display of skill, determination and sporting excellence. Teenager Kumkum Mohod clinched gold in the women’s individual recurve event at the Asian Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin in a dramatic shoot-off.After the final was tied 5-5, Kumkum shot a perfect 10 against Oh’s 8, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games medal in the individual recurve event. Earlier, Kumkum defeated China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2 in the semifinal to secure a quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.The quota is awarded to the country, and Kumkum became the first Indian recurve archer to assure herself of a medal in the women’s individual event.  In hockey, Defending champions India will take on against Malaysia, with the two teams meeting at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium with eyes on the gold medal and an LA 2028 Olympics quota.Yesterday, Indian Women’s Hockey team clinched the gold medal, defeating defending champions China 1-nil in the closely fought final. Lalremsiami Hmarzote scored the decisive lone goal for India, while goalkeeper Savita Punia produced a crucial save from a penalty stroke to preserve the lead and secure the gold medal. The victory marks India’s first women hockey gold at the Asian Games in 44 years, ending a long wait for the title. The Women’s Hockey team has also secured a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Earlier, Indian wrestler Sujeet Kalkal scripted a remarkable comeback to win the gold medal in the men’s 65-kilogram freestyle event. The 23-year-old Indian produced a stunning fightback in the final, recovering from a 4-9 deficit to defeat Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 and clinch the Asian Games title.With this victory, Sujeet has joined the elite company of Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, becoming the third Indian wrestler to win Asian Games gold in the men’s 65-kilogram category.In Boxing, Parveen Hooda won the gold medal in the women’s 65kg category, defeating Chinese Taipei’s Nien-Chin Chen 3-2 in a split decision in the final. Ankush Panghal clinched the gold medal in the men’s 80-kilogram category, defeating South Korea’s Kim Minseong by a split decision, 4-0, in the final.India’s star woman boxer Lovlina Borgohain also clinched a gold medal in the 75kg category, defeating China’s Bao Ziyi by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the final. It is India’s only second gold medal in women’s boxing at the Asian Games, following Mary Kom’s gold in 2014.In Archery, the women’s recurve team created history by clinching its maiden Asian Games gold medal. The trio of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod defeated world champions South Korea 5-3 in a thrilling final. India also bagged silver in the mixed recurve team event. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara finished runners-up after going down 3-5 to China in a closely contested final.In Sepaktakraw, India secured the bronze medal in the men’s quadrant event. The Indian team lost 0-2 to Japan in the semi-final but earned a place on the podium. In Sailing, Nethra Kumanan clinched bronze in the women’s dinghy event. The 29-year-old Indian sailor finished third with an overall score of 14 points.With these impressive performances, India has climbed to fifth position in the overall medal standings. The country’s medal tally has risen to 77, including 17 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.
